task.name: Design the first event-mix editing slice from shared iOS music work
task.description:
Outcome

Produce a bounded design for the first event-mix editing slice. Begin by surveying the existing iOS implementation, especially bach-performance-mirror, plus Ear reference-audio timing, Theory phrase variations, and the current MusicDocument. Reuse or unify those concepts before proposing macOS-only types. Keep the event mix as the proof and identify the smallest executable demo.

Required product model

* Every musical object can expose transport, waveform, loop selection, and further zoom into its structure.
* A song may derive four synchronized parallel voices: vocals, drums, bass, and other or instruments. Preserve the canonical original and provenance; separation is non-destructive.
* Analysis represents BPM or variable tempo, beats, downbeats, meter, key, confidence, and manual correction. Detected BPM is metadata; tempo automation and beat matching are reversible playback transformations.
* Sections and phrases are stable non-destructive source ranges with excellent waveform-first editing: suggested boundaries, audition, split, merge, labels, drag adjustment, and optional beat or bar snapping.
* A rollout remains one referential object such as phrase reference plus repetition rule and count or duration. The UI and renderer may materialize repetitions, but the document never denormalizes them into copied clips. Base edits propagate; iteration-specific changes remain overlays.
* Each object or transition has a local timing relationship: free preserves source time, snap aligns edit points without warping, and locked reversibly maps its beat grid to the parent mix grid. One mix may freely combine all three.
* Automation lanes target gain, tempo or playback rate, pitch, or effect parameters over musical time, support editable and preset curves, and remain typed, non-destructive, and serializable.
* Review every feature through both lenses: rhythmic mixing uses grid alignment, beat matching, synchronized overlap, and rollouts; spatial mixing uses silence, gaps, natural tails, overlap, and smooth volume glides. These are simultaneous lenses, not global modes. Space must be representable deliberately.
* The shared document, timing, automation, and phrase identity must work on iPhone and Mac. Platform UX may differ; semantics may not.

Deliverables and boundaries

Document the current-code inventory and reuse decisions, the minimum shared types and typed operations, the Mac and iPhone interaction seams, and the dependency boundary with Mix, Ear, Theory, Kata macOS, Music Agents, and Ableton. Name one thin executable demo and propose a small ordered set of follow-up Tasks with acceptance evidence. Separate decisions that require Jack taste from deterministic engineering choices.

Do not implement a general DAW, buy music, productionize source separation, build full Ableton round-trip sync, or hide the model behind a single mix-wide mode. Preserve unmixed and automixed sibling projections and a neutral Ableton handoff.

task.name: Tests never touch the live Loopflow home or inherit ambient LF_* state
task.description:
STANDING QUALITY FRONTIER, not a one-off. Tests must run against their own state — never the live `~/.lf` control-plane DB, and never with ambient `LF_*` / writer-authority env inherited from the Run that launched them. When they leak, the local gate passes but CI (or another machine) fails, and it looks like a flake instead of a missing boundary.

EVIDENCE (recurring):

* #1003 fixed one slice: ambient `LF_*` via EnvGuard's `AMBIENT_TASK_ENV`. Treated as a point fix, so the frontier has no owner.
* ci-fix on PR #1230 surfaced THREE more in one run: (1) a `git_operation` test saves the ambient writer token but never clears it; (2) a provider-broker test's spawned broker drops `LF_HOME` and reaches the live home; (3) a `wave_context` test opened this Run's live SQLite DB (0.12.13 draft) instead of its fixture.

INTENT — smaller, simpler, and more FLEXIBLE, so we get in our own way less. This is NOT 'lock every test in a rigid sandbox' and NOT more guards/allowlists. The leaks exist because the boundary is rigid in the wrong way: tests assume a fixed ambient home and each one opts out by hand. The fix is to make the system ADAPT to however it's launched — from a live Run, clean CI, or another machine — and resolve the right state for that context automatically, so a test just works wherever it runs. Flexibility over preconditions: fewer hard rules to satisfy, less ambient coupling, a smaller surface where a leak is even possible. Same through-line as 'accept any context, then adapt' (see the main-agents-move-off-canonical work).

PROOF that closes it: the full Rust suite run from inside a live Run/Task Session yields identical results to clean CI, with LESS isolation code than today — per-test scrubbing and the growing `AMBIENT_TASK_ENV` allowlist shrink or disappear because the system adapts to context instead of demanding tests conform to it.

See memory: cargo-test-inside-task-session.

task.name: Install local builds without destroying live work
task.description:
User outcome

A developer can promote a locally built main or branch through the protected installation transaction used by releases. The first local install uses a disposable clone of the reliable published store; compatible local builds reuse that clone. The installed CLI, daemon, keeper, macOS app, and helpers agree on the selected artifact and Home. A later published release returns to the reliable store without importing dev data. Promotion never destroys live work to make progress.

One promotion contract

* Route local and published artifacts through one machine-global promotion lock, exact preflight, activation, recovery, keeper restart, and health proof. Never copy or relink installed binaries around that transaction.
* Keep one reliable published store. A first local install clones it; compatible local installs reuse the dev Home; explicit fresh archives the old dev Home and reclones reliable data. Development binaries never receive reliable-store authority.
* Treat an exact complete artifact, app/helper, selected-store, migration-frontier, and settled-receipt match as a true no-op before any upgrade receipt, generation change, pause, signal, or reconciliation. Print already installed; fleet untouched.
* Before a real transition, settle absent owners only from exact Run-event and process-receipt evidence, then classify every live Invocation. Direct provider sessions may stop only with a proved native resume route. Same-lineage headless Work may stop only with a proved lifecycle relaunch. Captured first-fork Work may instead use the confirmed published-return or fresh parking disposition. Any other live or unprovable body defers the entire transition before pause or signal.
* Preserve typed HomeUpgrade causality. Same-lineage Work relaunches with RunTrigger HomeUpgrade and no retry lineage; confirmed rewind Work stays parked. Neither disposition creates a work-failure event or consumes Task or Project recovery.
* Use existing provider-session artifacts and command builders to reopen eligible conversations. Link old and replacement Invocations, preserve conversation evidence, and add no second inventory or handoff format.
* Record exact artifact, store, recovery, first-fork Work, and safe-stop disposition in machine-level promotion authority. Retain the complete published artifact set and reliable store as failback.
* A published return selects and migrates only the reliable store, parks surviving forked Work before reliable reconciliation, archives the dev Home for inspection, and never imports dev schema or rows.

Proof

One staged integration history proves: an exact reinstall leaves fleet identity untouched; local promotion clones but never mutates the reliable store; a live TUI or ambiguous owner defers promotion without receiving a signal; direct Claude and Codex conversations reopen from existing session artifacts; a headless Task relaunches across same-lineage local upgrades without spending recovery and is durably parked on published return; the 2026-08-19 stale Invocation shape settles exactly once with evidence preserved; keeper and app surfaces retain one artifact/store identity; failure injection leaves valid receipt-owned recovery; and the next published release migrates the reliable store once with no dev-data import.

task.name: [subsumed by LOO-55] Report the authoritative PR base without false contamination
task.description:
Found by W2-306 while diagnosing the re-mint base incoherence, and correctly left out of its scope. Filed by the Project because a Task session does not file its own follow-ups.

## The defect

ops/task.rs:1497-1511 classifies merge_base < base as:

'PR range is contaminated: recorded base carries commit(s) not on origin/main'

That is the #877/#882 foreign-ancestry case. It is FALSE for the mint bug. W2-300's row hits this arm — is_ancestor(9f6bdd498, 3e9df0677) is true — yet base 3e9df0677 IS origin/main's tip and carries nothing foreign. The message accuses the base of exactly the property it does not have, which sends a reader hunting foreign ancestry that is not there.

The arm conflates two distinct causes:

* (a) base is ON the upstream but AHEAD of the branch's fork point — the mint bug W2-306 fixes;
* (b) base is OFF the upstream carrying foreign commits — genuine contamination (#877/#882).

is_ancestor(base, upstream) separates them cleanly: true => (a), false => (b).

## Why this survives W2-306

W2-306 makes cause (a) unrepresentable going forward at the mint, and heals existing rows on adopt. So after it lands this message should become unreachable for (a) — but 'unreachable' is an assumption worth testing, not a reason to leave a lying diagnostic in the tree. Any future path that records a base ahead of the fork point lands here again and gets misdiagnosed.

## Done when

* The M<B arm distinguishes (a) from (b) via is_ancestor(base, upstream) and each names its real cause. A base that is the upstream's own tip must never be described as carrying commits not on the upstream.
* A test pins each arm separately with a fixture that actually has the property the message asserts. A single test over one shape passes with the conflation fully present — this is the same trap that hid the mint bug (a first-mint-only test is green while the defect is live).
* Do NOT change the fail-closed behaviour; only the classification and the text. Both arms still refuse.

## Context

Depends on nothing; W2-306 (#1059) may land first and is expected to. Read W2-306's design (scratch/a-re-minted-successor-pairs.md) for the base/merge_base model before touching this: base_commit == merge_base(upstream, branch) is the invariant the tree already states at ops/task.rs:1492 and 3455-3458.

task.name: [subsumed by LOO-55] Prove deterministic ci-fix recovery on the Run spine
task.description:
## Context

PRD-8 (product wave, "Wake a waiting Task into ci-fix when its PR fails") depends on four Infrastructure substrate tasks whose merged evidence was meant to satisfy its done-whens. All four are marked done in Linear:

* ENG-88 / W2-229 — Prove failed-PR ci-fix recovery as one deterministic lifecycle (#1009)
* ENG-20 / W2-230 — Route automatic ci-fix wakes through the durable Task command ledger (#1024)
* ENG-87 / W2-231 — Make ci-fix infrastructure failures block the Task actionably (#1001)
* ENG-19 / W2-232 — Settle one bounded ci-fix turn without entering the generic Task gate (#1063)

## The gap (found 2026-07-18 while auditing PRD-8 directive v4)

The architecture refactor #1073 ("establish the durable Run and Steer control spine") swept away two of the four implementations AFTER they merged:

* ENG-88's 2817-line deterministic lifecycle harness (`rust/loopflow/src/task/runner/ci_fix_lifecycle_tests.rs`) was **deleted** in #1073 and **not replaced**. Current ci-fix test coverage on main is only unit tests: `ci_fix_restart_bar_permits_only_a_failing_open_pr_wake` (1), `merge_gate*` (3), and `autonomy*` (4). No test exercises the full wake → fix → green → rearm path deterministically.
* ENG-20's durable command ledger (`ChildCommand` aggregate + `queue_command`) was **deleted** in #1073 via migration `0.11.035_drop_child_commands.sql`. The wake is now recorded through the `ci_incidents` store (`claim_ci_incident`, `mark_ci_incident_repaired`, `mark_ci_incidents_blocked`) on the Run/Launch/Basis spine. Whether that satisfies the "durable audited ci-fix command ledger" done-when needs a deliberate decision, not a silent replacement.

ENG-87 (blocked semantics) and ENG-19 (bounded settlement) survive in refactored form (`settle_ci_fix_turn`, `mark_ci_incidents_blocked` in `rust/loopflow/src/task/runner.rs`).

## What this task owns

Re-establish the deterministic lifecycle proof on the current Run/Launch/Basis architecture so PRD-8's original done-when #1 holds again:

> A deterministic integration harness opens a PR and proves: pending checks consume no body; one required failure starts exactly one ci-fix turn with canonical metadata; duplicate and multi-check deliveries coalesce; the fix pushes the same branch/PR and rearms observation for the new SHA; green CI does not wake a body; and an infrastructure failure produces an actionable blocker without code churn.

And confirm whether the `ci_incidents` store on the Run spine satisfies ENG-20's "durable audited command ledger" intent, or whether a dedicated audit record is still warranted.

## What this task does NOT own

The ci-fix wake mechanism itself (PR 967, product) and the blocked-semantics / bounded-settlement behavior (ENG-87, ENG-19). This is proof-and-audit restoration only, on the architecture that replaced the originals.

## Why PRD-8 stays open

PRD-8 directive v4 says: keep PRD-8 open and visibly dependent on the Infrastructure tasks until their merged evidence satisfies the original done-whens. The merged evidence no longer satisfies them because #1073 removed the proof. PRD-8 cannot close until this task (or equivalent proof) lands.

## Observed configured failure — 2026-08-21

The Product Wave committed durable memory on canonical main. Starting LOO-256 then failed before Task creation because main was ahead of origin/main. The refusal made the Wave’s own durable learning prevent all subsequent Task work.

## Proof

* In a temporary repository whose clean canonical main is one or more commits ahead of origin/main, `lf task run` creates the sibling Task worktree and bases it at the exact local canonical-main HEAD.
* No push, reset, force-push, origin equality check, allowlist, or manual reconciliation is required.
* Existing Task/worktree reuse remains idempotent.
* Landing still rebases/integrates through normal Loopflow PR mechanics.
* A newly authorized configured Task can be created from clean, unpublished canonical main without first publishing Wave commits; do not reopen completed LOO-256.

## Boundaries

This intentionally supersedes LOO-175’s fixed fetched-origin placement precondition while preserving its minimal-PR-range outcome. Remove the fixed-context precondition rather than extend it. Do not silently include uncommitted filesystem changes, mutate origin, or weaken Task/worktree ownership.

presentation.title: belief: add semantic belief formation and learning
presentation.body:
## Usage

```bash
uv run manabot belief-demo
uv run manabot belief-learn-demo
```

The first command exercises autonomous and explicitly supplied beliefs through the real agent path. The second trains an exact-world belief model and compares it with the combinatorial prior on held-out deals.

## Summary

This PR replaces the legacy positional condition channel with a first-class, viewer-safe belief lifecycle shared by policy/value inference and search. It also adds supervised exact-world learning from semantic public history, allowing a manabot to improve on managym's exact prior without exposing materialized hidden truth during inference.

## Changes

- Added normalized possible-world beliefs, typed query conditioning, revision-bound viewer history, and receipt-backed semantic encodings
- Routed autonomous decisions, explicit belief interventions, and conditional search through the same belief-aware policy/value state
- Bound belief-enabled checkpoints to their exact encoding schema and content manifest, failing closed on mismatches
- Added whole-world negative-log-likelihood training, episode-level held-out splits, frozen behavior-population provenance, and calibration and coverage metrics
- Extended managym's Python contracts for typed public commitments and reproducible possible-world fixtures and materialization
- Added runnable demonstrations and focused tests for deterministic inference, hidden-truth swap invariance, schema safety, and held-out improvement over the prior

# Restore Task watching with live session output and flow diagrams

## Accepted direction and execution

The human approved the attached draft in conversation and explicitly requested creating and advancing a Task, with the draft incorporated into the Task itself. This description embeds the complete draft and its open assumptions; it must remain sufficient after scratch is cleared.

Placement: Product wave, Desktop project. This resolves the draft's previously unresolved ownership. Build one end-to-end Task watcher, keeping live output and accurate stage diagrams together in one PR. Begin with the slice flow rather than repeating a kickoff conversation; retain the configured-path human demo gate before settlement.

Treat the native interactive transcript gap as required investigation and implementation within this Task, not permission to silently narrow the feature to autonomous Runs. Resolve the passive read contract in the Task design before dependent implementation. The accepted user-facing direction is Watch beside Changes and Terminal, a connected diagram of actual stages and attempts, one labeled feed across Task-attributed Runs, stage/Run filtering, Follow live, and inspectable completed history. Watching must never take over or interrupt an existing provider client.

Related work: LOO-291 joins Project/KR/Task planning to native Sessions. Consume its shared identities and navigation where available; this Task owns passive Task output watching and flow history, not a second planning or Session authority. Do not require that unrelated work to merge before investigating the watcher contract.

Implement and prove the complete design below, keeping current source/runtime differences explicit. Update the Task-local design as the native read contract is resolved. Do not claim all sessions are covered when an active supported interactive Session lacks passive output. Existing old Runs without retained evidence must show that limitation honestly.

## Resolved contract and remaining proof — 2026-09-23

This reconciliation supersedes draft-only API, placement, and implementation-status statements below while preserving the full accepted experience and pinned human/settlement gates. LOO-293 stays open under Product / Desktop; no remaining requirement is moved to a follow-up Task.

Committed foundation at 06ba29d57: Task-local events retain the immutable expanded invocation, exact stage/Run bindings, readiness/failure, Iterate/retry transitions, and settlement in the owning SQLite transactions. FlowPosition and its claim remain execution authority; inspection events never wake parent controllers. Passive native readers, launch/hook-owned source receipts, incremental output, file/stdin cursor transport, and the Rust/Swift output fixture are implemented. Concurrent Watch snapshot work is not validated by these foundation receipts.

Resolved passive contract: Rust reads Claude Session JSONL, Codex Session-matched rollout JSONL (including archived history), or exact OpenCode Session message/part rows through a read-only database. Resolve the recorded Session and exact account or the launch-owned native location stored in ProviderSessionRef; never select/refresh credentials, guess the observer's data root, or launch, resume, attach, replace, or interrupt the provider. Native records require source/item identity and revision beyond journal sequence numbers. TaskOutputPage groups ordered records and Run/provider/stage labels with availability/reset/gaps per TaskOutputSource. Normalize response items once, exclude event mirrors/internal instructions, and retain stable revisions for mutable parts. Source health belongs to output; missing plan/Run evidence belongs to the Watch snapshot.

The output command is `lf task output ISSUE --json [--cursor FILE]`; `--cursor -` reads stdin. Swift transports opaque values in a private temporary directory removed after success or failure. Input/output share a 4 MiB bound. OpenCode freezes the upper sweep timestamp and retains both inclusive boundary hashes and unfinished parts while paging; timestamp-only changes must not replay content. Partial JSONL tails wait; malformed/oversized complete records and resets remain explicit.

Remaining work in this same PR:

* Preserve native Claude/Codex call-result correlation through the shared shape and prove two same-tool calls returning out of order. Retain healthy Task output with explicit discovery uncertainty when unrelated manifests are malformed, missing, or disappear during reads. The concurrent foundation review reproduced both defects through synthetic CLI sources; repairs underway need their own focused proof.
* Complete autonomous/auxiliary tool-result capture (summary-only journals currently report limited_capture), faithful provider attribution across attempts, and configured Claude/OpenCode live proof. Prior Codex proof observed new prose/tools with the original owned client unchanged; it does not establish all-provider coverage.
* Separate historical paging from live continuation and bound discovery/retained state. Current discovery scans all manifests and flow facts on each query. Per-Run state, same-timestamp boundaries, and unfinished parts can hit the cap. Resolve or explicitly detect OpenCode backdated/equal-count completed-history rewrites; quiet output must not hide lost capture.
* Finish the shared Watch snapshot from one SQLite read transaction over position and ledger. Preserve expanded labels/ancestry, separate retries, exact return edges/settlement, active stage, auxiliary Runs, and explicit missing receipts. Do not fabricate a history cursor on an unpaged intermediate snapshot or mark interrupted/replaced attempts completed. Add Rust/Swift fixture and behavioral proofs.
* Finish Watch from Work, Roadmap, and Wave detail without worker/worktree prerequisites; filtering, Follow live across stages/Runs, older invocations/output, stale last-good evidence, accessible selection, visible-only polling/cancellation, and existing Session navigation.
* Prove autonomous and passive native output before completion, stage transition without reopening, previous-stage inspection then Follow live, concurrent auxiliary output, human Iterate with distinct attempts, and retained diagram/output after completion/reopen. Then enter the pinned configured human demo gate. Static diagrams, final-only output, terminal attachment, and autonomous-only coverage do not meet acceptance.

Prior file/stdin proof returned 469 distinct revisions and accepted a 2,186,420-byte padded cursor: transport capacity only, not realistic retained state or live arrival. Focused store/controller, native-reader, continuation, CLI/Swift transport, and DTO receipts are not a full Watch or release gate. Product / Desktop definitions and KRs do not change from this foundation.

## Incorporated draft design

# Task watcher

## What to build

Open any Task in the Mac app and watch its sessions' output arrive beneath a flow diagram that follows its actual progress, with earlier stages and attempts available to inspect.

User intent: “for any given task you were able to "watch" all the sessions output go by even as they were autonomous” and “we rendered flow charts for eac htask to show how it moved through stages.”

## Placement

Wave and Project unresolved: the seed names neither. This is a Task-level Mac visibility feature; no PM changes are needed to design it.

## Experience and demo

Add **Watch** beside **Changes** and **Terminal** in `TaskWorkspaceView`. Task entries in Work, Roadmap, and Wave detail expose the same Watch destination. Watching works without a live worker or surviving worktree. Changes and Terminal retain their existing prerequisites.

The upper pane shows the selected flow invocation as connected, selectable stage nodes. Show skill names, human checkpoints, operations, current state, and attempt counts. Group expanded steps by their existing flow ancestry. An Iterate transition draws a return edge to the stage actually revisited. Use text and icons as well as the existing status colors; support keyboard selection and reduced motion. Render the actual persisted plan, including custom flows; never hardcode the feature flow.

Below it, **All output** follows every Run attributed to the Task, including concurrent and auxiliary Runs. Label output with stage, Run, and provider; preserve each Run's event order and group contiguous output so parallel agents remain distinguishable. Auxiliary Runs stay visible without advancing the flow. Cross-Run ordering is observation order, not an assertion of causality.

Show streamed prose, commentary, commands, tool results, and failures. Long tool output can expand. A stage click filters to that stage's attempts; a Run click narrows further. Scrolling up suspends autoscroll. **Follow live** clears those filters and rejoins the live tail across stage and Run changes. An invocation selector exposes earlier flows after restart or serial PR work. Older output loads on demand.

Watch is read-only. Opening, closing, or reconnecting never resumes a provider, claims a Session, approves a checkpoint, or interrupts execution. A human checkpoint links to its existing interactive Session and decision controls.

Real demo: open Watch for a configured Task, see autonomous text and tool output, observe a stage finish and the next begin without reopening, inspect the previous stage, then follow live again. At a human checkpoint, open the existing Session and choose Iterate; see the recorded return path and separate attempts. Close and reopen after completion: the diagram and available transcript remain inspectable. Show a second concurrent Task Run in All output.

## Current system and evidence

Observed in this checkout, 2026-09-23:

* `TaskWorkspaceView.swift` offers Changes and Terminal and currently gates the entire workspace on runtime/worktree presence.
* `SessionRecord` represents interactive Sessions. Selecting one can launch/resume a native provider; it is not a passive autonomous output source.
* `session_command_status_with_env` in `lf/commands/util.rs` launches native clients with inherited terminal output and records client/session identity. The inspected path does not copy their conversation into Run events; the OpenCode observer extracts session identity only.
* `run_record.rs` stores sequenced, timestamped `events.jsonl`, including normalized conversation events, text/tool summaries, raw provider output, and outcomes. `RunSnapshot` has Task attribution and parent Run identity.
* `lf runs --task` silently limits discovery to seven days and approximately fifty Runs; `--events` reads one entire file. Neither contract supports complete, incremental Task watching.
* `FlowPosition` retains the expanded `QueuedInvocation`, cursor, iteration, and current worker/Session Run. Store mutations replace the cursor and delete the position on completion. `RunSnapshot` alone cannot identify historical stage occurrences.
* Historical commit `f56f457a0` (2026-02-08) added parsed live output and run history. At `c3bd1fdb3` (2026-03-30), `WaveDetailPanel` combined `LiveOutput` and `FlowProgressPills`. This is a close behavioral precedent, not confirmation of the exact remembered screen; the old surface was Wave-based.

## Data structures and ownership

Retain `FlowPosition` as execution authority and Run journals as output authority. Extend the existing Task event ledger with committed flow facts: invocation selected (expanded plan), stage entered, Run bound, decision/transition, and invocation settled or replaced. Write these in the same transactions as the corresponding position mutations, including human boundaries and completion. Keep these inspection facts local to the Task rather than triggering Project/Wave observations.

Identify stages by `(invocation_id, step_index)` and attempts by iteration plus Run identity. Bind from the owning transaction; never match by skill name or timing. The invocation's expanded plan is an immutable historical receipt, not another mutable flow definition.

Proposed read DTOs:

* `TaskWatchSnapshot`: Task identity, flow invocations/stages/transitions, attributed Runs, evidence availability, history cursor.
* `TaskOutputPage`: attributed output records, per-Run cursors, next history cursor, and explicit source gaps.
* Output identity: `(run_id, event_seq)`; retain turn/item identities for delta folding. Reuse existing conversation payloads where possible.

Every wire field is required or explicitly optional. Add Rust/Swift fixture coverage. Swift owns selection, folding, and scroll position; it owns no durable lifecycle state.

## Key functions and reads

Proposed commands: `lf task watch ISSUE --json` for the snapshot; `lf task output ISSUE --json [--cursor CURSOR]` for bounded incremental output and paginated history. These are read operations implemented over shared Run and Task readers, without the recent-Runs cap.

Proposed functions:

* Rust `read_task_watch(store, task_id) -> Result<TaskWatchSnapshot>`: join committed flow facts and attributed Runs.
* Rust `read_task_output(store, task_id, cursor) -> Result<TaskOutputPage>`: discover new Runs and read only complete new records, with bounded pages and opaque continuation.
* Swift `RegistryQuery.taskWatch(task:cwd:)` and `taskOutput(task:cursor:cwd:)`: typed CLI reads.
* Swift `TaskWatchStore.refresh()`: merge identities, fold deltas, retain selection and last-good evidence.

Poll while visible, initially once per second; cancel reads when hidden. Cursor state includes discovery progress and per-Run positions so new Runs join automatically. Incomplete trailing JSON waits for the next read; malformed complete records surface a gap. Reconnect deduplicates identities. Do not render normalized events and their raw provider copies twice. Pagination and delta folding must not require rereading the whole transcript on each tick.

## Constraints and forbidden outcomes

No revived daemon/WebSocket architecture, provider attachment for observation, direct Swift database/log parsing, fabricated completion from cursor position, or skill-name joins. Flow completion and Task completion remain distinct. A stale last-good view is labeled stale; absent output, unavailable source, and quiet live Run remain distinct. Older Runs lacking stage provenance remain inspectable as unassigned history. Do not reconstruct missing historical plans from today's YAML.

Native interactive transcripts are a separate capture gap. The full requested end state includes them; an autonomous-only release would be a smaller scope requiring an explicit decision. Investigate passive provider transcript reads using the recorded provider session/account identity, normalized in Rust, without taking over the client. Until that contract is designed and proved, this artifact is a restoration draft rather than a complete implementation handoff. Explicit unavailable-output states are failure handling, not satisfaction of “all sessions.”

## Internal slices and proof

This is one feature shipping as one PR: live output and the diagram must connect. Internal slices:

1. **This slice:** establish capture coverage and preserve exact invocation/stage/Run facts through current store mutations.
2. Implement bounded snapshot/output queries, historical paging, and reconnect behavior.
3. Build Watch, wire all Task entry points, and demonstrate the configured path.

Done when focused Rust behavior tests prove repeated skill names, retries, human Iterate, restart, and completion preserve exact attribution; incremental reads discover concurrent/new Runs without gaps or duplicates. Swift tests prove stage filtering and Follow live survive new output and transitions. DTO fixtures agree. A configured live demo proves autonomous text/tool output arrives before completion, then remains readable after reopening. A static diagram, final answers only, or an interactive terminal attach does not count.

Evidence ledger: source and historical inspection complete; native interactive capture gap identified; passive native read contract, implementation, and live demo pending. Review caught the native-output gap and the loss of completed flow positions; both are now explicit requirements. No follow-up Tasks created. Multi-task dashboards, graph editing, and remote transport expansion are outside this restoration.

## Incorporated open assumptions

# Task watcher assumptions

* Target is the current macOS Task workspace, inferred from the remembered UI. The user has not specified another surface.
* Proposed default is one combined, labeled feed with stage/Run filters; simultaneous split panes are not required by the seed.
* Wave/Project placement is unresolved because neither is named. No PM inspection or ownership mutation performed.
* Historical evidence finds Wave-level live output and connected stage pills in February–March 2026; the exact remembered screen is not confirmed.
* Autonomous Run event capture is present. The inspected native Session launch path inherits terminal output and records identity, without copying the conversation into Run events. Passive native transcript reads need a concrete contract before implementation can claim all sessions. The full requested scope includes that work; an autonomous-only first release is not assumed. Missing capture must not be disguised as an empty transcript or solved by taking over the provider.

## Data structures and key functions

### Optional conversations, one current at a time

User direction:

> “open a session with either the repo, wave, or proejct, but much like wiht a task you really only have 1 such session at a time, you only have the "one" session per level”

Each individual repo, Wave, Project, and Task offers an optional conversation, with at most one current user conversation at a time. Encourage bounded conversations and fresh starts. The durable subject persists independently of its conversations. The repo is a Session scope, not a new durable Work kind.

* Put Start conversation on the repo header, compact Wave/Project headings, and Task rows when no conversation is current. It starts fresh rather than automatically resuming the last historical conversation. Merely selecting a subject does not start a conversation.
* While a conversation is current, offer Continue and an explicit Start fresh. Continue returns to that exact conversation; Start fresh ends the prior ordinary conversation and begins a new one with fresh conversational context. Preserve prior history for deliberate access. Do not automatically replay old transcripts into fresh conversations.
* Finish conversation leaves the subject with no current conversation. It does not complete the Task, stop its autonomous work, remove its checkout, or close companion shells. A later Start conversation begins anew. Labels must distinguish conversation completion from Task completion.
* Repeated Continue actions across views/windows converge on the same Session identity. Starting fresh is an explicit lifecycle change, never a side effect of navigating. Client ownership still uses explicit Move here.
* The chosen Session can use A or D. Changing layout, hiding its view, or collapsing its parent does not finish it. Historical conversations are history rather than sibling current-session rows.
* Autonomous Runs remain independent execution evidence. Their presence does not consume or replace the subject's human Session.
* Repository-level exploration has a home before a Task exists. A repo Session can concern work in a checkout without that path becoming a Task or another hierarchy level. Do not infer Task ownership from cwd.

This supersedes the proposed standalone-Session/worktree inventory as the primary navigator. Do not add an “unfiled” queue or multiple current Session children under each subject. Worktrees own terminal grouping as designed in `lf-new`; they are not a fourth planning kind. Prefer that design's Task-first creation path for new implementation work. Existing unbound work still needs access and a non-destructive path into tracked work; do not silently create a second current repo conversation.

Existing Rust/Swift Session records already carry optional typed Work attribution, cwd, and stable Session identity; they do not yet establish this cardinality or a repo-session association. Shared start/continue/finish operations must own that relationship, not a Swift-only filter that hides extra live Sessions. Before implementation, reconcile existing multiple Sessions and Ask/FlowStep human boundaries: preserve pending decisions and history without silently closing, replacing, or hiding them. Optional conversation controls must not silently approve, iterate, or release a mandatory human boundary. Exact replacement/recovery semantics remain to be designed. No migration or API support is claimed by this sketch.

Next mockup: a repo Session, a Wave Session, a Project Session, and Task-owned autonomous/human work, all opened through their corresponding header/row. The separate Sessions-only window may become unnecessary once these paths have equivalent reachability.

### Existing shared values

Retain `RoadmapSnapshot`, `RoadmapTask`, `SessionRecord`, `WorkReference`, and `PodiumReading` as source values. `WorkspaceProjection` preserves Wave/Project nesting and each subject's optional current Session; a view-only `WorkspaceTask` carries one planning Task and its optional current Session. Its key uses repository plus planning Task id, so starting runtime does not change identity. Session identity remains stable independently of view placement. Expansion is a view-local set of typed node keys, separate from terminal layout and Work selection.

Proposed Swift seams:

* `projectWorkspace(roadmap: RoadmapSnapshot, sessions: [SessionRecord]) -> WorkspaceProjection`: associate by typed identity; retain unmatched Sessions explicitly.
* `selectWork(_ selection: WorkReference?)`: inspect without opening a provider.
* Proposed `startConversation(for: SessionTarget)`, `continueConversation(id:)`, and `finishConversation(id:)`: explicit shared lifecycle by repository or typed Work identity. Fresh replacement is a deliberate transition; exact backend API and recovery remain to be designed.
* Existing `SessionsStore.select(_:)`: open/focus the returned Session through its shared preparation path.

Planning Task ids and durable `runtime.workId` differ. Use the explicit shared relationship, never titles, branch names, or cwd guesses. Session identity remains its own id. Rust owns legal actions; Swift owns selection, filters, pane focus, and opening errors.

Fix Mac app Agent activity banner: activity --json decode misses `aggregate` key

The Mac app ([Loopflow.app](<http://Loopflow.app>) 0.12.8) shows a persistent warning banner in the Wave Fleet header:

> Agent activity unavailable
> lf query JSON did not decode: keyNotFound(CodingKeys(stringValue: "aggregate", intValue: nil), Swift.DecodingError.Context(codingPath: [], debugDescription: "No value associated with key CodingKeys(stringValue: "aggregate", intValue: nil)")

Where it happens:

* swift/Loopflow/Services/RegistryQuery.swift:349 throws RegistryQueryError("lf query JSON did not decode: ...").
* The failing call is the activity query: `workActivity(...)` runs `lf activity --since ... --limit ... --json` and decodes `WorkActivitySnapshot` (RegistryQuery.swift:120-133). The Swift DTO requires a top-level `aggregate` key that the CLI's `lf activity --json` payload does not emit (or emits under a different shape).

This is wire-DTO drift between the Swift mirror and the Rust emitter. Per STYLE.md's DTO rules: no defaults, every field required or explicitly Optional, and round-trip fixtures under tests/fixtures/dto/ must cover the shape.

Done when:

* `lf activity --json` output and the Swift `WorkActivitySnapshot` DTO agree on the wire shape (decide whether `aggregate` is required from the CLI or removed/Optional in Swift — align with what the Rust side actually emits and the fixture).
* The DTO fixture under tests/fixtures/dto/ covers the reconciled shape and both language fixture tests pass.
* The Mac app renders agent activity with no "Agent activity unavailable" banner against the live `lf` 0.12.8+ CLI.

One query, two shapes — a lens may change the SHAPE, not merely filter one outline:

No kanban board. The board metaphor is losing empirically (Vibe Kanban sunsetting, Crystal deprecated, Terragon shut down), and a board whose drag does nothing is a lie.

LOO-248 remained ready on existing PR #1231. A prior Project Run failed at the same boundary, so this is convergent evidence rather than a one-off launch race.

## Proof

* An integration path starts or steers a stopped Project from its Wave, durably applies the Steer, and gives the resulting Project Run a valid Basis before immediate-child Task control.
* The Project reserves or resumes the existing Task Run once; it creates no duplicate Task, worktree, Run, or PR.
* The exact-authority rule remains: Wave Runs still cannot control Task Work directly, and no ambient environment or provider process becomes authority.
* If a valid Basis cannot be established, status settles with one actionable non-convergence record rather than advertising resumable churn.
* The configured Product path can steer Loopflow API to resume LOO-248 without outside terminal intervention.

## Boundaries

Do not restore Session-controller identity, weaken immediate-child ancestry, or special-case LOO-248. Preserve Work → Epoch → Run → Turn authority and fix the generic Project relaunch/control path.

task.name: [absorbed] Fix Chrome focus stealing and login-server teardown
task.description:
Hotfix lf auth connect: stop 1 Hz Chrome focus-stealing and the 180s login-server teardown

Two defects in the managed login ceremony (`lf auth connect`), observed live on 0.12.8 while reconnecting accounts. Both block account recovery, which blocks wave/project runners fleet-wide.

Defect 1 — focus stealing (claude path):
`capture_claude_authorization_code_from_chrome` (rust/loopflow/src/provider_auth/mod.rs:1828) polls in a loop until CLAUDE_BROWSER_AUTH_TIMEOUT, executing CLAUDE_VISIBLE_PAGE_SCRIPT ([mod.rs:1864](<http://mod.rs:1864>)) every 1 second. Each iteration unconditionally runs:

* `tell application "Google Chrome" to activate` — yanks Chrome to the foreground every second, regardless of whether the auth window exists yet
* `perform action "AXRaise"` + synthesized `keystroke "a"/"c" using command down` — Cmd+A/Cmd+C land in whatever the user is typing in if focus shifts mid-delay
* clipboard save/restore each poll — races with any user copy during the ceremony

The user cannot use their machine while the ceremony runs. Fix direction: never `activate` in the poll loop. Query window existence passively (System Events window enumeration needs no activation); only when the matching "Authentication code | Claude Platform (<profile>)" window is present, do one activate+raise+copy pass. Better still, prefer reading the page without synthetic keystrokes if Chrome scripting allows.

Defect 2 — premature login-server teardown (codex path, reproduced today):
`connect` for authorization flows waits `tokio::time::timeout(AUTH_STATUS_POLL_TIMEOUT, handle.wait())` with AUTH_STATUS_POLL_TIMEOUT = 180s (lf/commands/auth.rs:36,379). On timeout, lf exits; the `.login-` tempdir drops and the AuthProcessGroup Drop (provider_auth/mod.rs:1798) SIGKILLs the codex login process group — including its localhost:1455 OAuth callback listener. A user still completing browser login then gets redirected to [http://localhost:1455/auth/callback?](<http://localhost:1455/auth/callback?>)... and sees ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED (reproduced 2026-08-19 with [manabot-eng@loopflow.studio](<mailto:manabot-eng@loopflow.studio>); nothing listening on 1455 afterward). The authorization code is orphaned and the account stays credential_state=missing.

180 seconds is far too short for a real login (password manager, 2FA, SSO redirects), and there is no env/config override (`wait_for_active_status` only honors provider expires_in). Fix direction: for interactive browser confirmation, wait the authorization-code flow window (AUTH_CODE_FLOW_TIMEOUT_SECS = 600 exists already at [auth.rs:40](<http://auth.rs:40>)) or until Ctrl-C, and print a clear "still waiting for browser approval (Ns elapsed)" heartbeat so the user knows the listener is alive.

Done when:

* During a claude connect ceremony, Chrome is activated at most once before the auth window exists and once to harvest the code; the user can type in another app for the entire poll window without losing focus or keystrokes (manual demo on macOS).
* A codex connect survives a slow login: with approval deliberately delayed past 3 minutes, the localhost callback still lands, the account flips to connected, and `lf usage` shows it. Reproduce the old behavior's failure in a test at the timeout boundary if feasible without a live provider.
* `lf auth connect codex manabot-eng@loopflow.studio` completes on this machine (the account invalidated since Aug 14 — the live victim).

task.name: Make release upgrades converge on an always-on Home
task.description:
# 5 Whys: An always-on Home cannot install a migration-bearing release

## The Problem

Installing the latest published release was refused because nine Runs were
non-ended, but an always-on Loopflow Home may never naturally reach zero Runs.

## Chain

Always-on Home cannot update -> every non-ended Run blocks migration -> install
has no quiesce/resume protocol -> the safety fix assumed a manual zero-Run
window -> installation is modeled as file replacement rather than Home
reconciliation.

**Problem**: The machine remained on `lf 0.12.4` while the Product demo needed
the `0.12.5` store frontier. Installing the published `v0.12.5` artifact found
nine active or stopping Runs and changed nothing.

**Why 1**: A migration-bearing promotion rejects every Run whose durable state
is not `ended`; the check does not mean an old process is currently writing.

**Why 2**: The installer can fence new Run reservations, but it cannot ask
resident Work to checkpoint, drain its process containment, or resume afterward.

**Why 3**: Promotion was hardened after a branch binary was installed behind an
incompatible shared-store frontier. The prevention correctly fails closed, but
its only safe state is a manually drained machine.

**Why 4**: At that point Loopflow did not have sufficiently durable desired
on/off state and restart reconciliation to preserve user intent through a
coordinated control-plane restart.

**Why 5 (Root)**: Updating Loopflow is treated as replacing CLI/daemon/app files
plus migrating SQLite, not as a Home operation that converges enabled Work onto
a new runtime generation.

## Unanswered Whys

| Branch Point | Unexplored Question | Priority |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Why 1 | Which non-ended Runs have live old-code containment, and which are only durable pursuit state? | High |
| Why 2 | What is the safe checkpoint boundary for Wave, Project, and Task Runs? | High |
| Why 3 | Which release migrations can remain backward-compatible for a rolling upgrade? | Medium |
| Why 4 | How should remote Homes coordinate a fleet update without a global outage? | Medium |

## Fixes

| Level | Fix | Prevents |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Immediate | Make the normal production updater download and promote the latest published artifact, exactly like an external install; keep current-main builds dev-local. | Maintainers accidentally treating unreleased `main` as production. |
| Structural | Add a migration upgrade operation that fences new Runs, checkpoints and drains live containment, promotes and migrates, then reconciles enabled Work. | Requiring a human to manufacture a zero-Run window. |
| Systemic | Treat runtime generation and upgrade state as Home reconciliation facts with durable receipts and restart policy. | Always-on operation and safe upgrades remaining contradictory goals. |

## Changes to Implement

- [ ] Replace main-pulling production refresh with latest-published-release
  resolution and the same signed-artifact promotion path external users take.
- [ ] Preserve an explicit dev-only source-build command that cannot become the
  production runtime while migration drafts exist.
- [ ] Distinguish durable non-ended Work from live old-generation process
  containment in promotion evidence.
- [ ] Persist Home upgrade intent and block new Run reservations for the old
  generation.
- [ ] Checkpoint and stop live Wave, Project, and Task bodies without changing
  their enabled flags, definitions, worktrees, or PM state.
- [ ] Promote CLI, daemon, and app; advance the migration frontier; restart the
  Home; reconcile every enabled Work item.
- [ ] Emit a typed receipt for drain, migration, restart, resumed Work, timeout,
  and rollback/failure state.
- [ ] Prove a migration-bearing release on an active Wave/Project/Task fixture
  resumes the same Work without an operator-created zero-Run window.

task.name: Make LLM-session checkpoints authoritative for Task landing
task.description:
## Problem

Managed Task work currently teaches two incompatible human surfaces. LOOPFLOW.md presents `lf pr submit` plus a GitHub merge click as the human shipping gate, while the Task lifecycle already creates durable interactive reviews inside provider-backed LLM sessions.

The lifecycle model is broader than one final Gate. Any `interactive: true` step in Kickoff, Iterate, or Gate may use `InteractionPolicy::Require` and block on a human in the existing LLM transcript. `Defer` assigns that same exercise to the owning Project LLM session. Therefore require/require/require, require/defer/require, and defer/defer/defer are all legitimate authored policies; they are not migration states to normalize.

GitHub UI review and a human merge click duplicate this model without its evidence, phase ownership, changes-requested transition, or recovery semantics. Conversely, arming `land` during Iterate can let merge outrun later required LLM-session checkpoints.

## User-visible outcome

A human conducts every required Task checkpoint by conversing in an LLM session, whether the checkpoint appears during Kickoff, Iterate, or Gate. The Task remains parked at that exact lifecycle step until the durable InteractionReview disposition resolves it. Project-deferred checkpoints happen through the Project LLM session using the same review protocol.

Managed Tasks never require the GitHub UI for review or merge. Agents publish PRs as evidence while work is in flight. Once the Task lifecycle has cleared every applicable required interaction, its approved settlement intent still matches current Task and PR evidence, and repository checks permit merging, Loopflow lands the PR mechanically. `changes-requested` resumes the correct owning phase without merge.

`submit` and `pr open` remain available only outside managed Tasks or when a human explicitly asks to inspect GitHub; neither is part of the managed Task lifecycle.

## End-to-end proof

Exercise managed Tasks against a real test repository and shared store:

1. A required Kickoff interaction parks in the Task provider transcript. Human follow-ups stay FIFO in that transcript; approval advances and changes-requested does not silently skip the Kickoff checkpoint.
2. A Task whose Iterate plan is `Require` parks on an interactive inner-flow step and cannot publish settlement or arm merge until that review resolves. A `Defer` Iterate routes the same exercise to the Project provider transcript.
3. Required Gate interactions run in the Task provider transcript. Changes-requested returns the same Session to Iterate; approval permits settlement only when the reviewed fingerprint remains current.
4. No managed path opens GitHub or waits for a human merge click. Iterate may call `lf pr publish`; `lf pr submit` and premature `lf pr land` are refused or excluded from Task prompts before lifecycle approval.
5. After all required lifecycle reviews clear, one replay-safe landing uses the recorded `-c` or `--next <slug>` disposition. CI failure keeps the PR open and invokes the existing repair lifecycle; green CI lets the merge queue settle it.
6. Restart during an LLM review or between final approval and land preserves the transcript, phase, disposition, and exactly-once landing action.

Prove this with focused Task runner/store/PR-operation tests and a CLI-level lifecycle exercise spanning required Kickoff, required Iterate, required Gate, changes-requested, restart, approval, and merge.

## Source of truth

The authoritative state is TaskLifecyclePlan and its per-phase InteractionPolicy, the phase cursor, durable InteractionReview conversation/disposition/evidence, TaskGateProposal settlement intent, and TaskPr publication/after-merge disposition. LLM prompts, CLI/Mac status, and recommended actions are derived views. GitHub review state is repository evidence, not human lifecycle authority.

## Affected surfaces and consumers

* Task runner transitions and review resumption in Kickoff, Iterate, and Gate
* Human and Project reviewer protocols in the existing provider-backed transcripts
* TaskGateProposal and TaskPr settlement intent, including replay-safe complete-versus-next landing
* Task-worktree authority for `lf pr publish`, `submit`, `open`, and `land`
* LOOPFLOW.md; task_clarify, task_pursue, task_mutate, review-design, demo, code-review, gate, land, and submit skills
* `lf task attach`, review message/reply/complete commands, Mac handoff presentation, status, and recommended actions
* CLI help, README, operations documentation, builtin prompt assertions, and lifecycle tests

## Absent and error states

No live provider body, missing reviewer, unresolved required review, changes-requested, stale evidence fingerprint, changed PR head, no PR, missing settlement disposition, CI failure, GitHub outage, failed land request, restart, and missing registry authority must each produce an actionable durable state. None may silently advance a phase, self-approve, open GitHub as a fallback, merge early, duplicate land, or wait on an unexplained merge click.

## Operational boundary

Review conversations and dispositions survive body replacement. Approval-to-land is replay safe across process death and network failure. The system never arms merge while any required lifecycle review is unresolved or while reviewed Task/PR evidence is stale.

## Exclusions

Do not remove GitHub PRs, weaken branch protection, eliminate `submit` for ordinary non-Task PRs, require one fixed interaction policy across all phases, add policy-selection UI, or redesign the generic provider terminal transport.

## Project KR

Directly advances: every dispatched task loop either lands its PR unattended after its LLM-session checkpoints clear or stops with an actionable non-convergence record, with zero silent stalls and zero human rescues through GitHub.

Incident evidence

During the current Product pursuit, several GLM/OpenCode bodies were hollow after an SSE disconnect. The work had to be handed manually to Claude Opus. Preserve the affected run/process/Task receipts as the reproduction corpus; do not infer the cause from the provider name alone.

Investigation and contract

* Identify where the SSE stream ended: OpenCode/provider transport, Loopflow harness decoding, timeout/cancellation, or account/model routing. Record model, provider, endpoint class, timing, last valid event, and terminal error without logging credentials or raw auth.
* Define an observable hollow-body boundary: no incorporated directive, durable mutation, useful assistant output, or explicit terminal disposition.
* Make pre-first-content and mid-stream disconnects produce durable failed/stalled body evidence with an actionable reason. Never turn EOF into success.
* Preserve Task/Project Session identity, provider history, worktree, commands, and generation fencing across recovery.
* Retry only when replay safety is proven. Otherwise route the next generation through the configured backup provider and retain the failed OpenCode generation as audit evidence.
* Keep the behavior in the shared OpenCode/harness and child-supervision contract, not Product-specific prompts or a GLM-name special case.

Proof

* A deterministic fake SSE server covers disconnect before headers/content, after metadata but before useful output, mid-tool call, and after a durable completion event.
* Tests prove exact body outcome, no false completion, one writer, no duplicate external side effect, and correct safe retry or backup-provider handoff.
* Replay the affected Product receipts and explain the root cause from evidence.
* Run at least ten GLM/OpenCode Product bodies with zero hollow successes; every forced disconnect is visible with reason and recovery owner.

## Evaluate

```bash
cargo test -p loopflow --test task_initialization_tests new_task_launch_rejects_an_unavailable_flow_before_persistence
```

The test passes after an unavailable loop flow produces a `flow not found` error naming the requested flow. It also proves that the rejected launch leaves both `tasks` and `task_prs` empty.

## Why it matters

A removed or renamed lifecycle flow must stop Task launch before durable state is created. Otherwise a configuration error can leave behind a managed Task or PR record for work that never started, complicating status and recovery.

task.name: Let an agent hand interactive work to a human and resume
task.description:
## User-visible outcome

An agent can deliberately open an interactive Codex, Claude Code, or other vendor session in the correct Home and worktree, block behind that exact session, and resume after the human completes or hands the work back. The same durable handoff can be opened from embedded Ghostty or a supported external presentation without creating a second agent or lifecycle.

## Contract

* Add one durable interactive child Session under the owning Wave, Project, or Task Session. Record parent, Home, worktree, provider, provider session id when available, body generation, reason human input is needed, and terminal outcome.
* W2-135 body leases and recovery remain authoritative. Build on its active PR rather than adding a parallel process owner.
* Launching the handoff atomically marks the parent as waiting for a human and blocks its flow at a replay-safe boundary.
* Expose a small attach descriptor with stable Session id, status, cwd, host, required environment, and terminal attach command or argv. Terminal bytes stay outside the API.
* Completion or explicit hand-back records durable evidence, terminates or adopts the child safely, and wakes the same blocked parent exactly once.
* Body death, app restart, host restart, repeated attach, and stale completion remain idempotent and do not orphan or duplicate the handoff.
* Keep non-interactive Wave, Project, Task, and direct execution bodies distinct. This primitive grants controls only to deliberate interactive handoffs.

## Historical implementation evidence

Rehome the lifecycle proven by commits c1d4adae8, f0eafbb18, 1267bf494, fbcf9f3af, c358e9cf4, 710bcd60c, and f0292d588 under the current store and Wave/Project/Task ontology. Do not restore lfd or the deleted parallel Session catalog from 309575f8e.

## Proof

Deterministic tests cover local handoff, repeated attach, parent process replacement, app restart, child body death, explicit hand-back, completion, and concurrent completion. Ten real handoffs open the exact same Session, preserve provider history and worktree, and resume the parent once. Shared DTO fixture tests pin the attach descriptor for Rust and Swift consumers.

## Delivery

Start this Task stacked on W2-135. The first PR owns the shared store and CLI contract plus tests. Mac Active Sessions and presentation adapters follow as separate Tasks.

task.name: Make Wave control-plane reconciliation self-healing
task.description:
## User-visible outcome

A running Wave continuously converges durable Project and Task intent with live process bodies, provider work, pull-request truth, and repository state. Users no longer see dead Projects counted as active, merged PRs described as open, or read-only commands rewriting their canonical checkout. After a laptop restart or body death, Loopflow either safely recovers the same work or names the exact boundary requiring intervention.

## Evidence to investigate

1. A live Product or Infrastructure Wave resident did not recover dead Project bodies.
2. Product reported five active Projects while every Project process was dead.
3. W2-135 continued to report PR #903 as open after GitHub had merged it.
4. Read-only Project turns refused to run when canonical main was dirty.
5. lf wt list invoked sync_main, auto-stashed existing edits, updated canonical main, and still returned a listing; additional edits then made main dirty again.

Preserve these as five deterministic reproductions. Do not collapse them into one generic stale-status bug before the ownership and event paths are mapped.

## Research questions

* Which durable record expresses desired Wave, Project, and Task intent, and which supervisor owns convergence for each level?
* What does active mean for intent, Session, body, provider turn, and child work? Which counts and labels should each product surface expose?
* Which event or observation reconciles GitHub PR state, and how fresh must it be before status may claim open, merged, failed, or review-required?
* Why do read-only Project turns depend on a clean mutable canonical checkout? Can they run against an immutable recorded base or repository snapshot while Task writers retain isolated worktrees?
* Which commands currently call sync_main or other mutating Git operations transitively? What public API makes read-only versus synchronizing behavior mechanically explicit?
* Which failures belong to automatic recovery, safe adoption, retry, NeedsInput, or terminal state under the W2-135 lease model?

## Source of truth

Durable Wave, Project, Task, directive, PR-sequence, and body-generation records in the Loopflow store own intent and identity. Process probes, GitHub, Git, and provider sessions are timestamped observations, not alternate identity. One reconciliation projection derives status, active counts, attention, next owner, and legal controls for CLI, roadmap, chat, and Swift.

## Product and API contract

* A live Wave supervisor periodically and eventfully reconciles every selected Project Session. It adopts a valid body, starts a safe missing body, preserves terminal intent, or records why recovery is unsafe.
* Desired active intent and observed live bodies are distinct typed fields. Counts must state which they count; a dead body can never make a live-process count positive.
* PR observations reconcile by stable PR identity and current head. A merge transitions the PR sequence exactly once and wakes the owning Project or Task decision path without waiting for a manual status probe.
* Read-only Project turns and inspection commands never require, clean, sync, reset, stash, fetch into, or rewrite canonical main. If fresh upstream state is required, the command names and owns that mutation explicitly.
* lf wt list and every other list, status, roadmap, doctor, diff, and file inspection surface are side-effect free. Add a mechanical command classification or boundary test so future transitive sync calls fail review and CI.
* Reconciliation is idempotent and restart-safe. Concurrent Wave, Project, Task, status, and external-observer events converge without duplicate bodies, lost edits, repeated PR transitions, or parallel intent.
* Every automatic action and refusal emits durable evidence with reason, freshness, next owner, and legal controls, feeding W2-123 rather than inventing a second presentation model.

## Affected surfaces and consumers

Wave and Project supervisors; Task/PR lifecycle; store schema and events; GitHub observation; Git/worktree operations; lf status, lf roadmap, lf project/task status, lf wt list, lf doctor; Wave Chat; Mac and iOS shared DTOs; builtin Wave/Project/Task skills; release and dogfood automation.

## Absent and error states

Missing execution context, unavailable GitHub, unreachable Home, ambiguous process ownership, dirty canonical checkout, stale observations, uncertain external side effects, and conflicting generations must remain explicit evidence. Never guess, report an empty healthy state, mutate main during inspection, or replay a control-uncertain action.

## Operational boundary

Reconciliation must remain bounded with no provider body required for mechanical adoption, liveness, GitHub refresh, or status projection. Read-only local commands should return promptly from persisted evidence and bounded probes. GitHub failure preserves the last observation with its age. A restart must converge without a human discovering the stall first.

## End-to-end proof

Run Product and Infrastructure with at least two selected Projects each. Kill every Project body, merge one waiting Task PR externally, leave canonical main dirty with named uncommitted edits, and invoke wt list, status, roadmap, and Project reconciliation concurrently. Prove:

* the Wave residents recover every replay-safe Project body exactly once;
* live-body and durable-intent counts remain distinct and correct;
* the merged PR advances once and reaches its owning decision path;
* all inspection commands leave HEAD, index, worktree, refs, and stash byte-for-byte unchanged;
* unsafe recovery becomes NeedsInput with exact evidence;
* CLI and Swift fixtures render the same state, reason, freshness, owner, and controls.

Repeat the scenario across process and laptop restart. Re-running reconciliation is a no-op.

## Delivery shape

One stable Task worktree and ordered serial PRs. Begin with a cross-layer design and deterministic reproductions. Expected slices are: reconciliation/source-of-truth model; Project-body recovery and active-count semantics; PR observation convergence; side-effect-free inspection and explicit sync APIs; shared status consumers and real two-Wave dogfood. Adjust boundaries when the code proves a simpler sequence.

## Relationship to existing work

Build on W2-135 body generations and write leases, W2-140 Project Session succession, W2-156 CI observation, and W2-123 visible-state semantics. Do not duplicate their models. If a required primitive is missing, extend its owning shared API in this Task's serial PR sequence and record the dependency.

## Exclusions

Do not pop or delete existing stashes, discard dirty work, create a second supervisor/store, or redesign GitHub review policy. Do not make canonical main writable by Project turns merely to bypass the read-only boundary.

## User-visible outcome

A Loopflow user opening Linear sees Cadenza work owned by the intended Cadenza team structure. Projects, Tasks, identifiers, and links agree with the repository and Wave that own the work; creating work through Loopflow cannot silently attach it to the legacy W2 team.

## Investigation

* Reproduce why Cadenza's Unified Practice Targets Project and W2-157 are associated with the legacy shared team even though the Cadenza Waves declare Linear team bindings.
* Establish whether Linear team ownership belongs to a repository, to each Wave, or to an explicit Wave-to-team mapping that supports both. Reconcile that decision with W2-155's one-team-per-Wave contract and the desired Cadenza experience.
* Audit the authoritative binding path from wave GOAL.md through the registry/database, PM sync, projectCreate(teamIds), task creation, doctor, roadmap, and Swift consumers.
* Determine whether the defect is stale configuration, incomplete rollout, unsupported cross-repository discovery, or a product-model mismatch.
* Inventory every affected Cadenza Initiative, Project, open Task, completed Task, and active Session before proposing mutation.
* Design an idempotent migration that repairs Linear Project team associations as well as Task teams, preserves stable provider UUIDs and live Session/PR ownership, and reports identifier changes.
* Identify why the shipped reteam path and lf pm doctor did not prevent or repair this state.

## Source of truth

The result must name one authoritative persisted mapping among repository, Wave, Linear Initiative, Linear team, and Linear Project. Linear display names, team keys, and issue identifiers remain presentation; stable IDs own identity. Every CLI and Swift view derives from the same mapping.

## End-to-end proof

From a clean Cadenza checkout, create or adopt one Wave, create a Project, and create a Task through Loopflow. The Linear Project appears under the decided Cadenza team, the Task receives the expected team prefix, lf pm sync/show/doctor agree, and roadmap/status links resolve to the same stable objects. Repeat against the current Unified Practice Targets data and prove the migration plan is a no-op on its second run.

## Absent and error states

Missing repository ownership, conflicting Wave bindings, inaccessible Linear teams, Projects attached to multiple or legacy teams, and active Tasks unsafe to move must stop with an exact diagnosis. No command may guess a team or partially move a hierarchy.

## Operational boundary

Discovery and dry-run are read-only. Any follow-on apply path must be restart-safe, preserve active Task Sessions and PR sequences, and expose every planned mutation before Linear side effects.

## Exclusions

Do not silently move existing Cadenza work during this investigation. Do not redesign Linear's workspace hierarchy, rename unrelated teams, or migrate completed history until the ownership policy and migration contract are explicit.

task.name: [retired] Wake a waiting Task into ci-fix when its PR fails
task.description:
User story

After a Task opens a PR, it sleeps without consuming a provider body while required checks are pending. If a required check fails on the current PR head, Loopflow wakes that same durable Task into a bounded `ci-fix` turn, repairs the existing branch, and updates the same PR. The user does not discover CI failures manually or rescue the worker from its worktree.

Lifecycle contract

* Pending checks are healthy waiting: persist the PR, head SHA, check state, and freshness, but run no provider body.
* A required check transitioning to failed on the current head enqueues one audited `ci-fix` turn for the same Task Session, worktree, provider history, and active PR sequence. Include PR number/URL, branch, head SHA, failing check names, and log URLs so the skill resolves the exact failure.
* Coalesce simultaneous failures and deduplicate wakeups by PR head plus observed failure set. A repeated poll or webhook delivery must not create two bodies or two fixes.
* The `ci-fix` turn follows the builtin skill: reproduce the latest failure, make the smallest correct fix, run targeted then proportional checks, and report an infrastructure or credential blocker rather than weakening tests.
* After a push changes the head SHA, return to sleep and watch the new checks. Green checks remain waiting for the configured review/merge action; a new failure may wake one new `ci-fix` turn.
* Manual `lf task resume ISSUE MESSAGE` remains a supported override for rebase or review feedback and must be consumed before the default open-PR waiting transition.
* Preserve the exactly-one-body/write-lease rules and expose pending, fixing, blocked, and green-with-next-owner truthfully through `lf status`.

Operational boundary

Use the existing Task event/command path and builtin `ci-fix` skill. Do not add a second CI worker identity, duplicate Task, new worktree, provider transcript, or CI-specific monitor store. GitHub check evidence is authoritative only for the PR current head; stale failures never wake work.

Proof

A deterministic integration harness opens a PR and proves: pending checks consume no body; one required failure starts exactly one `ci-fix` turn with canonical metadata; duplicate and multi-check deliveries coalesce; the fix pushes the same branch/PR and rearms observation for the new SHA; green CI does not wake a body; and an infrastructure failure produces an actionable blocker without code churn. Reproduce W2-144 generation 7 to prove a queued manual repair is incorporated once instead of being discarded because the PR is open.

## Infrastructure dependencies

The full done-whens remain open until these substrate tasks merge and their evidence is incorporated:

* W2-229 — deterministic failed-PR ci-fix lifecycle proof
* W2-230 — durable audited ci-fix command ledger
* W2-231 — actionable Blocked semantics for infrastructure failures
* W2-232 — bounded ci-fix settlement without generic gate re-entry

PR #967 may ship as an incremental Product slice; it is not task-completion evidence by itself.

task.description:
## User story

As a Loopflow user browsing Linear, I can identify the owning Wave from a Task identifier alone: PRD-* for Product, INF-* for Infrastructure, and INT-* for Intelligence. Creating, moving, and running work through Loopflow preserves the Wave → Project → Task hierarchy without funneling every Task into one shared W2 team.

## End-to-end contract

* Persist an explicit Linear team binding per Wave alongside its Initiative binding. Stable provider IDs own identity; team display names and keys remain mutable presentation.
* Make `lf pm init` create or adopt the intended Wave team and requested key, diagnosing conflicts instead of guessing.
* Associate Linear Projects with the owning Wave team and create every new Task in that team.
* Provide an idempotent, restart-safe migration for current W2 Tasks. Preserve issue UUIDs, descriptions, comments, relationships, PR links, ordering, completion, and Loopflow Task and Project Session ownership while updating visible identifiers wherever they are cached or displayed.
* Protect live and in-review Tasks during migration. Prove that a Linear team move is safe for an active Session or defer it explicitly; never strand a worktree, PR sequence, provider history, or durable Session because W2-123 becomes PRD-123.
* Make and document one deliberate policy for completed W2 history: preserve it as historical or migrate it with traceable identity.
* Keep Linear team keys and prefixed Project display names separate from Loopflow Wave and Project identity. Repo slugs, cache keys, and command inputs must not derive from provider presentation.
* Keep CLI, status, chat and roadmap links, Swift DTOs, docs, and `lf pm doctor` consistent with the same mapping.

## Proof

* Product, Infrastructure, and Intelligence each create a real Task through Loopflow and receive PRD-, INF-, and INT- identifiers respectively.
* A dry run names every issue that will move, every identifier that will change, and every protected Task it will defer.
* Migration preserves open and completed work, active Session lookup by stable issue ID, PR associations, Project membership, and task ordering.
* Re-running setup and migration performs no duplicate team, Project, Task, or move.
* A cross-Wave move either completes safely with a traceable identifier change or refuses with an exact recovery action.
* PM sync and doctor finish cleanly, and the Linear workspace is visibly grouped by Wave without changing Loopflow repo names.

task.name: Recover an abandoned Task without losing its work or PR history
task.description:
User story

When a Task attempt is abandoned because its provider, process, or execution context is unsafe, the user can deliberately recover that same durable Task without losing its worktree, serial PR history, directives, or audit trail—and without Loopflow silently restarting terminal work.

Current product model

A Linear Task may ship through multiple serial PRs. The Task is durable intent; Task Session attempts and process bodies are execution history. Completed Tasks and merged completion PRs never relaunch. Failed or interrupted work resumes the same safe Session. Abandonment requires an explicit recovery decision.

Contract

* Offer one explicit recover action for an abandoned Task. It creates a linked successor attempt only when the stable worktree and next serial PR can be adopted safely; otherwise it requires a new Task and explains why.
* Preserve predecessor/successor history, Task directives, existing PR sequence, branch/base evidence, and pinned execution context. Never create parallel active attempts or parallel active PRs.
* Converge concurrent recovery requests on exactly one non-terminal attempt.
* Integrate with the leased-body supervision model: automatic process recovery may replace a body, but terminal abandonment is never crossed automatically.
* Expose actionability in CLI and shared Now/Roadmap DTOs: recover, resume, start next PR, complete, or no legal action, with reason and owner.

Proof

End-to-end tests cover interrupted resume, safe abandoned successor, unsafe legacy context, concurrent recover, submitted Task, multi-PR Task between PRs, and completed Task. One dogfood Task is abandoned and deliberately recovered through its next PR with one worktree, one active writer, complete history, and no manual database or Git repair. Depends on the shared supervision contract in W2-135.
